partC_zahlen.decisiveFinding: THE ZAHLEN COLLISION IS NOT PRIMARILY A CASE PROBLEM. a1-3 authors { de: "Zahl", plural: "Zahlen" } (line 285), so the inflection index maps the LOWERCASE key "zahlen" to the NOUN lemma Zahl. KW_INFLECTIONS is inherently lowercase-keyed, so making WORDIDX case-sensitive would NOT stop "Zahlen, bitte!" resolving to the noun — the lemma path would still reach die Zahl.
partC_zahlen.consequence: Candidate 1 is INSUFFICIENT for Zahlen, and possibly for any noun whose authored plural collides with a verb infinitive. This is a class of defect, not one word.
partC_zahlen.corroboration: chapter/conj-migration-inventory.json already records lemma "zahlen" as a known KW_INFLECTIONS conflict ("conflicting Präsens-shaped form(s): zahlte") — the project had independently flagged this word.
partC_zahlen.nounUsesThatMustNotRegress: 8 authored noun occurrences across c1-35, c1-19, c1-32, b2-10, c1-21, c2-09, c1-04 — every one carries an explicit authored role/type, so they resolve through the token path and are NOT exposed to the surface-guess path that produces the a1-15 defect. That is the key safety result: the 8 noun uses are insulated by their authoring.
partC_zahlen.verbUsesThatMustResolveAsVerb: a1-15 vocab entry (line 259), a1-42 token (line 430, authored r-verb), c2-19 token (line 209, authored), and the 2 rendered a1-15 occurrences that are currently WRONG
partC_zahlen.verdict: a case-aware index alone does not fix Zahlen. expectedClass (Candidate 2) would: the a1-15 occurrences carry r-verb, which is class-incompatible with the Noun entry, so the existing guard would reject it.
partC_zahlen.confidence: PROVEN for the inflection-index mechanism and the authored-token insulation (both read from source). The live resolver behaviour was NOT executed.

partE_byDesignControl.wouldCandidate2ChangeThem: NO — and the reason is structural: expectedClass only REJECTS entries whose word class contradicts the occurrence. The 15 by-design pairs are family refinements (adverb→negation, adverb→question, verb→modalverb), which classesCompatible treats as compatible, so no entry would be rejected and no resolution would change.
partE_byDesignControl.wouldCandidate1ChangeThem: NO for Nein/Nicht/möchte/muss (no case-pair authored). Wann is capitalised and sentence-initial in its occurrence — a case-sensitive index COULD alter its resolution. NOT TESTED.
partE_byDesignControl.wouldCandidate3ChangeThem: POSSIBLY — sentence-position resolution is exactly the signal that would affect capitalised sentence-initial Nein and Wann. This is the strongest argument against Candidate 3 without a full regression.
partE_byDesignControl.verificationMethod: reasoned from the compatibility rule and the authored data, NOT executed against a live resolver
partE_byDesignControl.confidence: STRONGLY SUPPORTED for Candidate 2; UNVERIFIED for Candidates 1 and 3
